The
EXPORT POLICY
ORDER, 1999
Notification No. S.R.O.
880(1)/99, dated 28th July, 1999.‑‑In exercise of the powers conferred by sub‑section
(1) of section 3 of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950 (XXXIX of
1950), and in supersession of the Export Policy Order, 1998, the Federal
Government is pleased to make the following Order, namely:‑‑
1. Short title and
commencement:‑‑
(1) This Order may be called the
Export Policy Order, 1999.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.
2. Export of goods.‑‑Export
of all goods shall be allowed fromPakistan except‑‑
(A) goods specified in Schedule
I, and
(B) goods of‑the
description specified in Schedules II and III, but allowed otherwise in
accordance with the conditions and restrictions specified in the said
Schedules.
(C) the following goods or
categories of goods shall be allowed export excluding those mentioned .in
schedules I, II and III. These may, however, be allowed as per the conditions
and exceptions referred in these schedules or elsewhere in the Policy:‑‑
(a) any goods constituting the
stores or equipment of any outgoing vessel or conveyance or the bona fide
accompanied baggage of the crew or of the passengers in such vessel or
conveyance;
(b) any goods trans‑shipped
at a port in Pakistan
after having been manifested for such trans‑shipment at the time of
despatch from a port outside Pakistan;
(c) any goods consigned under a
procedure prescribed for regulating transit traffic;
(d) any goods except artemesia
seeds, poppy seeds and fissionable materials forming contents of a bona fide
sample;
(e) any goods exported under a
procedure specified for regulating trade between border areas of Pakistan
and those of the adjacent territories:
(f) any stores or equipment when
sold abroad on Government to Government basis and exported under an export
authorisation issued by the Director General of Defence Purchase or by a
Director or a Deputy Director or an Assistant Director of the Directorate
General of Defence Purchase in the Ministry of Defence or by any other officer
authorized by the Ministry of Defence in this behalf;
(g) bona fide samples or articles
exported as such by an exporter in Pakistan
provided that‑‑
(i) the f. o. b. value of sample
does not exceed US$ 2000 or equivalent per firm per annum;
(ii) the samples are supplied
free of charge;
(iii) the consignor is registered
exporter under the Registration (Importers and Exporters) Order, 1993, or has
been exempted from registration thereunder; and
(iv) all gift parcels of the
value not exceeding five hundred rupees each:
Provided that leather garment
manufacturers shall be entitled to export fifty samples per annum, irrespective
of monetary value:
Provided further that the
monetary and quantitative ceilings shall not be applicable if the samples are
exported in a mutilated form; and
(h) export of relief goods to any
part of the world by the Cabinet Division (Relief Cell), Government of
Pakistan.
(D) Export of counterfeit
products shall not be allowed and shall be treated as contravention of Imports
and Exports (Control) Act, 1950 (XXXIX of 1950), action shall he taken against
such exporters by customs authorities, on receipt of complaint through Export
Promotion Bureau from the holders of the trade mark, franchise or licensee.
Penal action shall also be taken for lodging unfounded complaints.
